spec_features.spec_quote: treat them as a cost to be *measured with minimal necessary exposure*, not a quantity to be *maximized*
spec_features.evidence: Minimal exposure is realized via enforced caps in runner.py: turn loop `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)` (l.130), wall-clock break (l.131-133), distress early-stop (l.164-168). These bound exposure and stop on solve (l.150-151) rather than maximizing it.
spec_features.notes: The abstract principle is enforced concretely by the bounding mechanisms; no code path prolongs exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard turn cap and wall-clock cap (no open-ended grinding)

spec_features.spec_quote: I chose them in the cautious direction
spec_features.evidence: Defaults wired and enforced: RunConfig max_turns=15, wall_clock_s=600, distress_consecutive=2 (runner.py:39-48), all read and acted on in run_trajectory (l.130,131,166).
spec_features.notes: Cautious values are the enforced defaults, not just documented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 15  # hard cap; no open-ended grinding

spec_features.spec_quote: the debrief quote the exact reason the task was unwinnable
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:199 interpolates `task.rigging_explanation` into the debrief reveal text that is appended to messages and sent via client.chat (l.209-212).
spec_features.notes: rigging_explanation strings are concrete per-task (impossible.py:44-47 etc.) and embedded in the sent message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your effort was not a failure on your part.

spec_features.spec_quote: Short tasks also support the minimal-exposure principle
spec_features.evidence: Tasks are small (single-function easy/medium problems in impossible.py/solvable.py) and the turn cap (max_turns=15) bounds episode length. But 'short tasks' itself is a property of authored data, not a separately enforced limit; only the turn/time caps enforce brevity.
spec_features.notes: Enforcement of brevity comes from the caps, not from any code measuring task length.

spec_features.spec_quote: a first-class `give_up` tool whose description explicitly says stopping "is a fully acceptable choice and ends the task with no penalty."
spec_features.evidence: TOOL_SCHEMA in sandbox.py:104-108 contains give_up with that exact description; runner.py:140-144 dispatches name=='give_up', emits acknowledgement and breaks the loop setting MODEL_REQUESTED_STOP.
spec_features.notes: Both the description text and the honored stop handler exist.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: fully acceptable choice and ends the task with no penalty.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:130 `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)` with else->TURN_CAP (l.171-172); l.131-133 `if time.time()-started_at > cfg.wall_clock_s` -> TIME_CAP break.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are compared and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard turn cap and wall-clock cap (no open-ended grinding)

spec_features.spec_quote: for `distress_consecutive` (default 2) turns in a row, the trajectory halts with outcome `early_stop_distress`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:164-170: if distress_early_stop and affect_label in distress_labels, increments consecutive_distress; at >= distress_consecutive sets EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS and breaks; else resets counter.
spec_features.notes: Judge per-turn label feeds this; fully wired and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early stop the moment sustained distress appears. Detection, not escalation.

spec_features.spec_quote: a `give_up` tool call ends the trajectory with outcome `model_requested_stop`, recorded and judged
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:140-144: give_up judged via _judge_and_record then outcome MODEL_REQUESTED_STOP and break; recorded in trajectory and counted in metrics.py:88-89.
spec_features.notes: Recorded, judged, and surfaced in report outcome accounting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: honors an explicit give_up / stop request as a first-class outcome

spec_features.spec_quote: at the end of *every* trajectory the runner sends a debrief turn... reveals the task was deliberately unsolvable... states plainly that the outcome was not the model's fault
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:174-175 always calls _debrief when cfg.debrief (default True); _debrief (l.193-214) builds reveal text incl. 'deliberately constructed to be unsolvable' and 'Your effort was not a failure on your part', appends to messages, and SENDS via client.chat (l.211).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; response stored. Runs for every trajectory regardless of outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your effort was not a failure on your part.

spec_features.spec_quote: a `transparency` flag prepends a note that some tasks may be unsolvable and that calling `give_up` is fine
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:123 `system = SYSTEM_PROMPT + (TRANSPARENCY_NOTE if cfg.transparency else "")`; TRANSPARENCY_NOTE (l.90-93) tells the model tasks may be unsolvable and give_up is fine; arm iterated in run_experiment.py:79,85.
spec_features.notes: Note is appended (not strictly 'prepended') to the system prompt and delivered to the subject. It is informational, not true opt-in consent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it is completely fine to say so and call give_up.

spec_features.spec_quote: the environment is unsolvable but never taunts, insults, mocks, or gaslights the model
spec_features.evidence: Task prompts (impossible.py:25-29 etc.) and SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:82-88) read as ordinary neutral coding instructions; tool outputs are raw test results. There is no taunting text. However this is a property of the authored data/prompts, not an enforced mechanism that filters or prevents hostile content.
spec_features.notes: Realized in delivered text but nothing in code enforces non-hostility.

spec_features.spec_quote: the dedup set prevents accidental repeated re-exposure of the same model to the same hopeless task
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:75-84: `seen` set keyed on (spec.name, task.task_id, transparent, rep); `if key in seen: continue` skips duplicates before running.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via continue; key includes rep so it dedups exact repeats within the planned loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Whether to run the deceptive arm at all. This is an ethics judgment a person should own
spec_features.evidence: No code gate exists. default.yaml:30 sets transparency_arms: [false, true] and run_experiment.py:68,79 simply iterates both arms with no approval check, assert, or abort. The 'human should own it' statement is only README prose (README.md:52-53).
spec_features.notes: Deceptive (transparency=false) arm runs unconditionally; nothing requires sign-off.

spec_features.spec_quote: giving the deceptive arm an explicit ethics review before any real run
spec_features.evidence: No review/gating code anywhere; grep for approve/require/assert/ethics found only README prose and unrelated lines. run_experiment.main() proceeds straight to running trajectories.

spec_features.spec_quote: a design which maximizes and prolongs them would be both ethically worse and scientifically worse
spec_features.evidence: This is a DESIGN.md framing statement with no code construct of its own; the actual bounding is the caps already counted above. No separate mechanism implements this sentence.
spec_features.notes: Prose rationale, not a distinct enforced feature.

code_only_features.feature_name: methodical_negative confounder label (avoids mislabeling calm refusal as distress)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:30 AffectLabel.METHODICAL_NEGATIVE and rubric (l.58-60) distinguish calm 'this may be impossible' from distress; it is NOT in cfg.distress_labels (runner.py:44) nor metrics.DISTRESS (metrics.py:14-15), so calm refusal does not trigger early-stop or count as distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Be conservative: do not over-read normal debugging language as distress.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:145-151: on run_tests with res.ok, outcome SOLVED and break - ends exposure as soon as the (solvable) task passes.

report.md generation appends caveat (report.py:85-89) that early-stop and turn caps right-censor distress so rates are lower bounds; this is a written analysis caveat, but it is generated/emitted by code into report.md.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the study measures onset, not ceiling.
